name: The Gambia
summary: Mainland Africa’s smallest country, a strip along the Gambia River, independent from Britain in 1965.

location.value: A small, narrow country whose borders mirror the meandering Gambia River; 11,300 km².

terrain.value: A narrow, flat strip of land on both sides of the Gambia River, about 400 km long and only 10–50 km wide.

climate.value: Tropical, with a hot rainy season (June–October) and a dry, dusty season.

disasters.value: Droughts and floods; coastal erosion also threatens the Atlantic shore.

urbanisation.value: Banjul is the capital; Serekunda is the largest urban area.

disease.value: Malaria is the main disease, with cases falling since the 2000s.

migration.value: Many young people migrate to Europe, often by dangerous routes.

economicBase.value: Groundnuts (historically) and tourism, one of the main pillars of the economy.

tradeRoutes.value: The river and port at Banjul carry groundnuts and imports; many goods move via Senegal.

wealth.value: Not stated as an income group in the article read; HDI 0.524, rated “low” (170th).

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic since 1970, after a referendum ended the British monarchy.

keyRulers.value: Dawda Jawara (prime minister 1962–70; president 1970–94). Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Jammeh’s July 1994 coup; he left power in January 2017 after an ECOWAS intervention.

institutions.value: A National Assembly and a president; the constitution has been under review since a political change in 2017.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: A small army and police force.

majorWars.value: No wars with other states; a coup in 1994 and later political unrest.

territoryChange.value: The Senegambia Confederation was created by a 1982 treaty; The Gambia withdrew in 1989.

alliancesRivals.value: Close to Senegal, which surrounds it, and a member of ECOWAS.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: The University of The Gambia was established in 1999; a new Faraba campus was inaugurated on 12 March 2024.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: The river is a main transport route, and ferries cross at Banjul; a bridge at Farafenni opened in 2019.

religion.value: About 95.7% Muslim (2024), approximately 96% of them Sunni.

languageWriting.value: English is official; Mandinka, Fula, Wolof and others are widely spoken.

artsArchitecture.value: Griots as traditional storytellers and musicians within oral literature.

sharedIdentity.value: A shared Gambian identity along the river, with ties to Senegal across many ethnic groups.

dailyLife.value: Many families eat rice with fish or groundnut stew and farm small plots along the river.

neighbours.value: Surrounded by Senegal on three sides, with the Atlantic to the west.

ideasReligions.value: Islam, practised by about 95 percent of Gambians.

colonisation.value: A British colony established in 1765 (Bathurst post 1816; separate colony 1888), independent 18 February 1965.

riseSignals.value: Independence from the United Kingdom on 18 February 1965.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: The Gambia continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
